newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ericsson Brazil unit to boost capacity.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson Brazil unit to boost capacity.

text.p: Swedish giant Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson's Brazil unit said it plans to invest $30 million and double output capacity to one million cellular phones a year by the end of 1998 at its new Sao Jose dos Campos plant.

Carlos de Paiva Lopes, board president of Ericsson Telecomunicacoes SA, said the company has already spent $20 million on the factory and plans to invest another $10 million in the plant in the second half of this year.
The plant began production in March, with an initial output capacity of 500,000 cellular phones a year.

President and CEO of Ericsson group worldwide Lars Ramqvist told reporters that Brazil would soon become Ericsson's fifth largest market. Brazil currently ranks as the company's seventh biggest market.
"We have no other ambition than to be the leading telecommunications company in Brazil," Ramqvist said at a news conference.
He said the company expects business in Brazil to grow by 30 percent to 35 percent in the coming years as a result of the Brazilian market's liberalization.
Ericsson is part of a consortium bidding on Band B cellular concessions, which are due to be awarded by the end of June.
Ericsson posted 600 million reais in sales in Brazil last year and held 10 percent of the country's cellular market in the period.
Lopes said that the company hopes to grow to control 30 percent of the analog cellular market and 40 percent of the digital cellular market in the coming years.
